Point $M$ is the midpoint of the arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$. Connecting $BM$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. $AD$ bisects $\angle CAB$ and intersects $BM$ at point $D$, and $D$ is the midpoint of $BM$. What is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct $MH\perp AB$ at $H$, connect $AM$, $OM$, where $OM$ intersects $AC$ at $F$. \\
$\because AB$ is the diameter,\\
$\therefore \angle AMB=90^\circ$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAB+\angle CBA=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ point $M$ is the midpoint of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$,\\
$\therefore \overset{\frown}{CM}=\overset{\frown}{AM}$\\
$\therefore \angle CBM=\angle ABM$,\\
$\because \angle CAD=\angle BAD$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAB+\angle DBA=\frac{1}{2}(\angle CAB+\angle CBA)=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB=180^\circ-(\angle DAB+\angle DBA)=135^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle ADM=180^\circ-\angle ADB=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore MA=MD$,\\
$\because DM=DB$,\\
$\therefore BM=2AM$, let $AM=x$, then $BM=2x$,\\
$\because AB=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore x^2+4x^2=20$,\\
$\therefore x=2$ (the negative root has been discarded),\\
$\therefore AM=2$, $BM=4$,\\
$\because \frac{1}{2}\cdot AM\cdot BM=\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot MH$,\\
$\therefore MH=\frac{2\times 4}{2\sqrt{5}}=\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\

$\because \overset{\frown}{CM}=\overset{\frown}{AM}$,\\
$\therefore OM\perp AC$,\\
$\therefore AF=FC$,\\
$\because OA=OB$,\\
$\therefore BC=2OF$,\\
$\because \angle OHM=\angle OFA=90^\circ$, $\angle AOF=\angle MOH$, $OA=OM$,\\
$\therefore \triangle OAF\cong \triangle OMH\left(AAS\right)$,\\
$\therefore OF=OH=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\
$\therefore BC=2OF=\boxed{\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

$\because AB$ is the diameter,\\
$\therefore \angle AMB=90^\circ$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAB+\angle CBA=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ point $M$ is the midpoint of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$,\\

$\therefore \angle CBM=\angle ABM$,\\
